profile.summary: ViroCaduceus is a DNA language model built by the ViroBench authors to test whether a virus-enriched pretraining corpus helps nucleotide models on viral tasks. It takes a Caduceus backbone and trains it on ViroBlend (also spelt ViroBland), a 216 Mbp mix of human, multi-species and viral sequence. Given a DNA sequence it returns hidden states, which the benchmark pools into embeddings for viral taxonomy and host classification.

summary_quotes.text: -based (Mamba-DNA) nucleotide language model pre-trained on the **ViroBlend** (ViroBland) corpus, a small (216 Mbp) mixed pretraining dataset with source-wise stratified sampling to balance human reference, multi-species genomes, and viral in-domain sequences.
applying the same ViroBland pre-training strategy to DNABERT2 and Caduceus-PS, resulting in ViroDNABERT2 and ViroCaduceus.
These results suggest that the benefit of ViroBland is not tied to a particular architecture
Frozen backbone encoder + lightweight supervised head (for classification)

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: ViroCaduceus uses the Caduceus (Mamba-DNA) architecture. The paper describes it as Caduceus-PS adapted with the same ViroBland pretraining used for the authors' ViroHyena models. The released file is a set of backbone weights. To use it, the demo script loads the Caduceus-Ph base model from kuleshov-group, then overlays the ViroCaduceus weights from pytorch_model.bin. It tokenises the sequence, takes the last hidden layer and mean-pools over non-special tokens to give one embedding per sequence. In ViroBench the backbone is frozen and a light supervised head is trained on top for classification.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One checkpoint is published, YDXX/ViroCaduceus; this page read revision 91cee313. The paper also calls it Caduceus-ViroBench. Its sources disagree on the base: the paper says Caduceus-PS, while the model card and the demo script use Caduceus-Ph. The repository's config.json is a HyenaDNA configuration (d_model 32, 2 layers), which does not match a Caduceus model with d_model 256, so a result should name the revision and the base model used to load the weights. The demo script only applies the ViroCaduceus weights if YDXX/ViroCaduceus/pytorch_model.bin exists on disk relative to where it runs; otherwise it silently returns the unmodified base model.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Caduceus (Mamba-DNA). The model card says Caduceus-Ph with d_model 256; the paper says Caduceus-PS.

quotes.text: applying the same ViroBland pre-training strategy to DNABERT2 and Caduceus-PS

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A DNA sequence, upper-cased and tokenised with the Caduceus base tokenizer, truncated to 1024 tokens in the demo script.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Per-token hidden states; the demo script mean-pools the last layer into one embedding per sequence.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: Not reported. Hugging Face gives no parameter count; the weights file pytorch_model.bin is 31,001,682 bytes.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: ViroBlend (ViroBland), 216 Mb: selected GRCh38 intervals (3.01 Mb), multi-species genomes from the Nucleotide Transformer dataset (163.84 Mb) and viral sequences from the OpenVirus (LucaVirus-Gene) corpus (49.01 Mb). After deduplication it has 32,023 training, 4,000 validation and 2,662 test sequences.
facts.source_locator: Paper section 4.2.4, Pre-training corpus and Table 7; model card

quotes.text: ViroBland is a 216M-nucleotide pre-training dataset designed to combine broad genomic context with virus-enriched in-domain information.
Selected intervals from GRCh38 (Chr1–22 and ChrX), providing stable eukaryotic genomic context.
covering bacteria, fungi, invertebrates, and vertebrates.
A curated subset from the OpenVirus (LucaVirus-Gene) corpus, providing high-density viral nucleotide sequences.
After sequence-level deduplication, the final ViroBland corpus contains 32,023 training sequences, 4,000 validation sequences, and 2,662 test sequences.

strengths.text: The ViroBench authors report that ViroCaduceus improves on Caduceus-PS in every column of their classification ablation, with the largest gains in taxonomy prediction.

quotes.text: Caduceus-ViroBench improves over Caduceus-PS across all columns in Table
The improvement is particularly pronounced for taxonomy prediction

strengths.text: The pretraining corpus is published, so the data behind the model can be inspected.
A short demo script produces a sequence embedding and falls back to CPU when no GPU is found.

limitations.text: No licence is stated for the weights or the code, so terms of reuse are unclear.
The sources disagree on the base model (Caduceus-PS in the paper, Caduceus-Ph in the card and script), and the bundled config.json describes a HyenaDNA model.

quotes.text: applying the same ViroBland pre-training strategy to DNABERT2 and Caduceus-PS

limitations.text: The demo script loads the ViroCaduceus weights only if it finds YDXX/ViroCaduceus/pytorch_model.bin on local disk, and loads them with strict=False. If the file is missing it runs the plain base model without warning.
It was built as an ablation inside a benchmark paper, and the training protocol is written out only for the ViroHyena models, not for ViroCaduceus.

run_guide.summary: Install the dependencies, get the model repository at a pinned revision and run the demo script to embed a random DNA sequence with ViroCaduceus.
prerequisites: Python with torch, transformers, mamba-ssm and causal-conv1d, as the model card lists. No versions are given.
The script uses a CUDA GPU if one is available and the CPU otherwise. GPU type and memory are not stated.
No licence is stated for the weights or code.
Network access to download the kuleshov-group Caduceus-Ph base model, which the script loads with trust_remote_code=True.

The clone and checkout lines and the changed script path were added by this page, as explained in each step.
If the weights file is missing the script prints an embedding from the base Caduceus-Ph model without any warning.

notes: The paper says ViroCaduceus was built from Caduceus-PS, but the model card and get_embedding.py use the Caduceus-Ph base, and config.json is a HyenaDNA config; worth a human look before results are attached. The ViroBench README does not mention ViroCaduceus; script/run_all.py loads it as caduceus-virobench from a hard-coded local path, so it was not used for the run guide. The paper (CC BY 4.0) is the model's own primary source here, as well as being the existing benchmark source lit-microbial-20261011-virobench-source-ye2026.
